description: The anchor of the on-stack half of the handler-boundary rule. spec/execution-model.md:660-664 gives two reasons a handler's `return`/`stop` must be reported rather than obeyed, and this is the first: "a `return` in a handler firing while the registering call was still on the stack would be consumed as that call's own result". The `wait` is INSIDE `setup`, so the firing happens while `setup` is still on the stack, and the `stop` must raise `ol-stop-outside-proc` (spec/error-model.md:119) rather than quietly ending `setup` — measured, an implementation that lets it through emits a `procedure-exit`, no diagnostic, and never reaches `print 99`. Added at the QA reviewer's request during review round 4, which measured that the conversion is written out ONCE PER HANDLER KIND in four separate functions, and that removing it from `invokeEveryHandler`, `invokeOnKeyHandler` or `invokeOnClickHandler` — one at a time — survives all 1038 fixtures. Four hand-copied blocks are a classic copy-paste divergence site, and this repository has already shipped exactly that regression once: `interaction-events/on_key/on-key-body-runs-in-registration-environment`'s own description records a defect in `invokeEveryHandler` surviving the whole corpus because the property was asserted for one kind only. Its siblings cover the remaining kind/signal cells.
